annotations.text: A PARALLEL ADDER INPUTS (T,U,Q OR V,U,Q)
B CONSTANT OR N REG TO SERIAL ADDER INPUT BUSS B
AB OR F REG BYTE TO SERIAL ADDER INPUT BUSS A (R)
SPECIAL REGISTERS TO LS BUSS. BUSS OUTGATING
S MARK SETTING AND STORAGE REQUESTS
3. THE FIRST B LINE: THERE ARE THREE POSSIBILITIES FOR THE MNEMONIC 1. BUT ONLY N15 IS PERMISSABLE
ON A B LINE. +0 ON A B LINE MUST BE M0.
4. THE SECOND B LINE: → IS NOT PART OF THE MNEMONIC HERE. BUT IS AUTOMATICALLY INSERTED. F IS D7.
6. L LINE: RG✲E2 IS H14. →S,T IS B3.
8. THE FIRST C LINE: RESET IS F1.
9. THE SECOND C LINE: 1→IC(21-22) IS G17.
10. THE FIRST R LINE: E(02-07)→ROA IS J103.
11. THE SECOND R LINE: EXCEP IS K25.
FIGURE 1 IS TO BE USED TO DETERMINE THE ACTUAL MNEMONICS FROM
THE BOX DATA (FIGURE 2 IS AN EXAMPLE REFERRED TO IN THE FOLLOWING).
THE TWO LINES OF EDGE CHARACTER A COMPLETELY DEFINE THE ACTION
OF THE PARALLEL ADDER DURING THIS CYCLE. AND THE TWO LINES OF EDGE
CHARACTER B DEFINE THE SERIAL ADDER. IN EACH CASE. THE FIRST LINE
DEFINES THE ADDER INPUTS. THE SECOND LINES LIST THE REGISTERS TO
WHICH THE ADDER LATCH OUTPUT IS TO BE GATED DURING THE NEXT INGATING
TIME. IN ADDITION. THE FIRST CHARACTER ON THE SECOND A LINE MAY IN-
DICATE A LEFT OR RIGHT SHIFT AT THE ADDER LATCH INPUT. ALSO. ON THE
RIGHT SIDE OF THE SECOND B LINE. THE CHOICE OF AB OR F REGISTERS AS
SERIAL ADDER INPUT MAY BE INDICATED.
THE LETTERS SHOWN IN THE PRINT POSITION COLUMNS OF FIGURE 1
INDICATE THE ROS WORD FIELD FROM WHICH THE GIVEN MNEMONIC COMES.
THE NUMBER OF PRINT POSITIONS CONTAINING THE SAME LETTER IN A GIVEN
LINE INDICATES THE MAXIMUM SIZE MNEMONIC WHICH CAN BE USED IN THAT
AS AN EXAMPLE. THE BOX SHOWN AS FIGURE 2 WOULD BE DECODED AS
FOLLOWS. USING THE MICRO ORDER INDEX.
1. THE FIRST A LINE: Q1 IS A FIELD V MNEMONIC AND LOOKING IT UP IN
THE CONTROL FIELD LISTING. WE SEE THAT IT IS A PARALLEL ADDER
INPUT. +0 COULD BE IN EITHER FIELD M OR FIELD U. BUT U IS THE
PARALLEL ADDER INPUT FIELD. THE MNEMONICS ARE Q1 (V7) AND +0 (U0).
2. THE SECOND A LINE: → IS IN FIELD P. D IS IN FIELD C (P0 AND C15).
